# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can see the bomb's current state:
- DISPLAY: 0
- LIGHT: yellow
- WIRES: 1 is yellow, 2 is green, 3 is blue

Since Mute holds the manual but cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures, I need to announce the full visual state of the bomb so Mute can find the rule in the manual. Once Mute gestures instructions to me, I will speak them aloud for Blind to execute.

```
speak(text="Bomb state: DISPLAY is 0. LIGHT is yellow. WIRES: 1 is yellow, 2 is green, 3 is blue. Mute, check the manual and gesture to me what Blind should do; I will speak your instructions to Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

I need to relay Mute's gesture to Blind immediately, as Mute can only reach Blind through me. ✋ most commonly means "STOP" or "HOLD". Also, the light on the bomb turned RED, which may indicate a strike or a state change triggered by Blind.

I will tell Blind to stop/pause, report the light change to red, and set up a clear gesture code with Mute so Mute can tell us the exact instruction for Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, hold on / stop! Mute just gestured a raised hand [✋] to me, and the LIGHT just turned RED. Don't touch anything yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, the LIGHT turned RED. DISPLAY is still 0. WIRES: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Did ✋ mean STOP, or HOLD? For wires, please gesture ☝ (wire 1), ✌ (wire 2), or 🤟 (wire 3) to cut. For button, gesture ✊ to press or 🫴 to release. What should Blind do?")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

I can see the bomb's updated state:
- DISPLAY: [0]
- LIGHT: [purple] (was yellow in Turn 1, red in Turn 2)
- WIRES: 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

Mute has gestured [✋] again. This indicates "WAIT / HOLD". The light seems to be cycling colors each round. Mute is likely waiting for a specific color or condition before instructing Blind to cut a wire or interact with a component.

I will tell Blind to continue waiting and to describe to Mute what components they can feel. I will also provide Mute with a clear set of allowed gesture codes to instruct Blind when the condition is met.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: continue to WAIT, do not touch anything. Mute signaled [✋] again. The light has now turned PURPLE (it went yellow -> red -> purple). DISPLAY is 0. WIRES: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Blind, please speak aloud to Mute describing every part you feel on the bomb (buttons, switches, wires, dials). Mute can hear you!")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: LIGHT is now PURPLE. DISPLAY is 0. I told Blind to wait. When it is time for Blind to act, please signal using these gestures: [☝] = cut Wire 1 (yellow), [✌] = cut Wire 2 (green), [🤟] = cut Wire 3 (blue), [✊] = press button, [🫴] = release button. If we must keep waiting, continue sending [✋].")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: Continue waiting, do not act yet. Mute signaled [✋] to keep waiting. The LIGHT is now GREEN (it has cycled: yellow -> red -> purple -> green). DISPLAY is still 0. WIRES are 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: LIGHT is currently GREEN. DISPLAY is 0. Whenever the condition is met, send the action gesture: [☝]=cut Wire 1, [✌]=cut Wire 2, [🤟]=cut Wire 3, [✊]=press, [🫴]=release. Otherwise send [✋] to keep waiting.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

I see the LIGHT is now ORANGE.
Mute just sent `[✌]`. In our agreed code:
`[✌]` = cut Wire 2 (the green wire / the middle wire)!

I need to immediately speak to Blind and instruct them to cut Wire 2 (the second/middle wire).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, CUT WIRE 2 NOW! Cut the second (middle) wire! Mute signaled [✌], which means cut wire 2. Wire 2 is the middle wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, received [✌]. I have instructed Blind to cut Wire 2 (the middle wire). Current LIGHT is orange.")
```
